title: The iterator dies mid loop
summary: From erase-remove on a vector to erase's return value on a map, then folded into one erase_if template.

turns.user: the loop that drops finished jobs crashes sometimes, and it also leaves some behind. is ++it after erase the problem

assistant.body: Step 1: erase on a vector invalidates every iterator at or after the erased slot, so the ++it right after it advances a dead iterator. On top of that it throws away the next position erase returns, so the scan skips one element each time. That is where the leftovers come from. For a vector the erase-remove idiom folds it into one call.

turns.user: there is a std::map<JobId, Job> doing the same thing. fix that one too

assistant.body: The same shape works. Hand std::remove_if the map's begin and end, then erase from the returned position to end. One idiom, both containers written the same way.

turns.user: does not compile. pages of noise about assigning to value_type

assistant.body: Important correction, and my apologies: that was wrong. std::remove_if shifts the kept elements forward by move assignment, and a map's key is const, so it cannot be used there at all. A node based container takes the next iterator that erase hands back instead.

turns.user: we are on C++20, why not just std::erase_if. and I want one name for both

assistant.body: std::erase_if absorbs that difference. The standard ships an overload per container, so a vector and a map take the identical call. Let's fold it into a template that takes the predicate and returns how many went away.

turns.user: actually drop the return value, void is fine. and rename it sweep_if

assistant.body: The return goes, the name changes, and both size calls become dead, so those lines get deleted outright. The d command in sed deletes a matching line, and the . inside the pattern is escaped so it does not stand for any character.
sed -i '' 's/std::size_t purge_if/void sweep_if/; /const auto before = container\.size();/d; /return before - container\.size();/d' src/sched/purge.h
Callers no longer need to know which container they hold. Nothing left in here cares about iterator invalidation.
